title: 스토킹범죄 사건의 심리 및 재판 등에 관한 규칙 / queue:ARTICLE:2:0:00002:part:1/1
title_original: 스토킹범죄 사건의 심리 및 재판 등에 관한 규칙
full_text:
Article 2 (Procedures for Hearing Opinions)
(1) Where a court deems it necessary to hear the opinions of a prosecutor, a stalker, a victim, or another person for reference (hereinafter referred to as a "person concerned") before making, pursuant to Article 9 (3) of the Act, a decision to order the provisional measures prescribed in Article 9 (1) 3-2 or 4 of the Act, a decision to change another type of provisional measure to either of the foregoing measures, or a decision to extend the period of the provisional measure under Article 9 (1) 3-2, the court shall set a hearing date and hear the opinions of persons concerned: Provided, That where special circumstances exist, such as a risk of harm to the victim, the court may require persons concerned to submit written statements of their opinions.
(2) Where a court decides to hear the opinions of persons concerned by the method prescribed in the main clause of paragraph (1), it shall promptly notify the persons concerned and the prosecutor of the hearing date orally, by telephone, facsimile, electronic mail, mobile text message, or any other appropriate method, in addition to written notice. In such cases, proof of notification may be made by recording the fact of notification in the hearing record.
(3) The prosecutor may appear and state an opinion at the hearing referred to in the main clause of paragraph (1).
(4) Where opinions are heard pursuant to the main clause of paragraph (1), a court official participating in the hearing shall prepare a hearing record. The hearing record shall include a summary of the statements of the persons concerned.
(5) Where a court deems it necessary, it may conduct the hearing referred to in the main clause of paragraph (1) through video relay facilities or an Internet video system. Article 123-13 of the Rules of Criminal Procedure shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods of such a hearing, to the extent not inconsistent with its nature.
